text: An LCR circuit contains resistance of 110$\Omega$ and a supply of 220 V at 300 rad/s angular frequency. If only capacitance is removed from the circuit, current lags behind the voltage by 45${}^{\circ }$. If on the other hand, only inductor is removed the current leads by 45${}^{\circ }$ with the applied voltage. The rms current flowing in the circuit will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the capacitor removed, the LR circuit has the current lagging by $45^{\circ }$:

$\tan 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{X_{L}}{R}\Rightarrow X_{L}=R=110\Omega$

With the inductor removed, the CR circuit has the current leading by $45^{\circ }$:

$\tan 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{X_{C}}{R}\Rightarrow X_{C}=R=110\Omega$

In the full LCR circuit $X_{L}=X_{C}$, so the circuit is at resonance and

$Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+(X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}=R=110\Omega$

$I_{rms}=\dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z}=\dfrac{220}{110}=2\text{A}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

solution.body:
[IMG]

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}}=\frac{\cos ^{2}β}{\cos ^{2}α}$

text: Consider the diffraction pattern obtained from the sunlight incident on a pinhole of diameter 0.1 $μ$m. If the diameter of the pinhole is slightly increased, it will affect the diffraction pattern such that:
options: its size increases, but intensity decreases
its size increases, and intensity increases
its size decreases, but intensity increases
its sizes decreases, and intensity decreases
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Yes, you're absolutely correct. This equation you provided is for the angular size of the central maximum (or central diffraction disk) in a circular aperture diffraction pattern (like a pinhole) :

$\sin θ=\frac{1.22λ}{D}$

where :

θ is the angle subtended by the radius of the central maximum at the pinhole,

λ is the wavelength of the light, and

D is the diameter of the aperture or pinhole.

If D (the diameter of the pinhole) is increased, then sinθ (and hence θ itself, for small θ) will decrease, implying that the size of the central maximum or diffraction disk will decrease. This is because less diffraction (bending of light) occurs when the pinhole is larger.

At the same time, increasing the size of the pinhole allows more light to pass through, which increases the intensity (brightness) of the light in the diffraction pattern.

So, increasing the diameter of the pinhole decreases the size of the diffraction pattern but increases its intensity, which confirms Option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

text: Y = A sin($ω$t + $𝜙_{0}$) is the time-displacement equation of a SHM. At t = 0 the displacement of the particle is $Y=\frac{A}{2}$ and it is moving along negative x-direction. Then the initial phase angle $𝜙_{0}$ will be:

[IMG]

$𝜙_{0}=π-\dfrac{π}{6}=\dfrac{5π}{6}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The peak electric field produced by the radiation coming from the 8W bulb at a distance of 10 m is $\frac{x}{10}\sqrt{\frac{μ_{0}c}{π}}\frac{V}{m}$. The efficiency of the bulb is 10% and it is a point source. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Firstly, we know that the intensity (I) of a wave is defined as the power (P) per unit area (A). For a spherical wave emanating from a point source, the area of the sphere is $4πr^{2}$ where r is the distance from the source. So, 

$I=\frac{P}{4πr^{2}}$ ........(1)

This intensity can also be related to the electric field (E) in an electromagnetic wave using the equation : 

$I=\frac{1}{2}cε_{0}E^{2}$ .........(2)

where $c=\frac{1}{\sqrt{μ_{0}ε_{0}}}=$ speed of light in vacuum and $ε_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space.

From equations (1) and (2), we can solve for E and square root it to find the peak value of the electric field $E_{\text{peak}}$ :

$E_{\text{peak}}=\sqrt{\frac{2P}{cε_{0}4πr^{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2Pμ_{0}c}{4πr^{2}}}$

Since $ε_{0}=\frac{1}{μ_{0}c^{2}}$

Given the efficiency of the bulb is 10%, the actual power radiated is $0.10\times 8\text{W}=0.8\text{W}$. 

So, substituting $P=0.8\text{W}$, $r=10\text{m}$, $c=3\times 10^{8}\text{m/s}$, and $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\text{T m/A}$, we have :

$E_{\text{peak}}=\sqrt{\frac{2\times 0.8\times 4π\times 10^{-7}\times 3\times 10^{8}}{4π\times 100}}=\frac{x}{10}\sqrt{\frac{μ_{0}c}{π}}$

Comparing with the expression in the question, we find that $x=2$.

 Therefore, the answer is $x=2$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift

tan$θ$ = $\frac{kq^{2}}{mgr^{2}}$

$q^{2} =$ $\frac{\tan θmgr^{2}}{k}$

$\because$ tan$θ$ $\approx$ sin$θ$ = $\frac{0.1}{0.5}=\frac{1}{5}$

$q^{2}=\frac{1}{5}\times \frac{10\times 10^{-6}\times 10\times 0.2\times 0.2}{9\times 10^{9}}$

$q=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\times 10^{-8}$

after comparison from the given equation a = 20

text: Two particles having masses 4 g and 16 g respectively are moving with equal kinetic energies. The ratio of the magnitudes of their linear momentum is n : 2. The value of n will be $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ relation b/w kinetic energy & momentum is

$P=\sqrt{2mKE}$ ($\because$ KE = same)

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{n}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{16}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $n=1$

text:
A current of 6A enters one corner P of an equilateral triangle PQR having 3 wires of resistance 2$\Omega$ each and leaves by the corner R. The currents $i_{1}$ in ampere is $_________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


The current $i_{1}=\left (\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}\right )i$

$=\left (\frac{2}{4+2}\right )\times 6$

$i_{1}=2A$
